$note: THE ONE PLACE A LINK LIVES. Every outbound purchase or read link on the Books system is configured here and nowhere else - never inside content/books/*.json, never inside a template, never in assets/js. A book only ever records WHICH providers it is available on through this file; changing a URL, adding a provider or retiring one is a single edit here and a rebuild. scripts/books_engine.py resolves this file into (a) the provider buttons rendered on books.html and book-<id>.html and (b) the internal redirect stubs under go/book/<id>/<provider>.html, which is what the site links to - the raw URL never ships in a book page or in data/books.json.

settings.$note: Applied by the engine to every external target it writes. `query` is merged into the target's query string (existing keys win, so a URL that already carries a parameter is never clobbered). `amazonAssociateTag`, when set, is written as Amazon's `tag` parameter - leave empty until the Associates account is live.

futureProviders.$note: Reserve for the next network (Agoda, EarnKaro, a direct advertiser). Add the id here, add its label/host/external, then give books a URL under `books.<id>.<new-id>` - the engine picks it up with no template, component or build change. Nothing below is wired to anything yet.

books.$note: book id -> provider id -> destination URL. A book id with no entry, or a provider with an empty/absent URL, is simply NOT AVAILABLE: the engine renders 'Currently unavailable' for it instead of a button. Order follows `providers` above, so adding a network reorders every button consistently.
